qt: to the Commission Mónica Silvana González (S&D) Subject:

With a budget of nearly EUR 80 billion for the period 2021-2027, the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NIDICI) ‘Global Europe’ covers more than 70 % of the EU’s external relations funding. It is based on three pillars: geographic programmes, thematic programmes and rapid response actions. The thematic pillar will fund support for human rights and democracy, civil society, stability and peace, with an envelope of EUR 6.36 billion. The budget for civil society organisations (CSOs) is EUR 1.36 billion. What are the criteria and standards utilised in the selection process to determine the allocation of funding to the beneficiary organisations?
at: (English version) to the Commission Mónica Silvana González (S&D) (13 March 2024) Subject: Financing of civil society organisations under the NIDICI With a budget of nearly EUR 80 billion for the period 2021-2027, the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NIDICI) ‘Global Europe’ covers more than 70% of the EU’s external relations funding. It is based on three pillars: geographic programmes, thematic programmes and rapid response actions. The thematic pillar will fund support for human rights and democracy, civil society, stability and peace, with an envelope of EUR 6.36 billion. The budget for civil society organisations (CSOs) is EUR 1.36 billion. What are the criteria and standards utilised in the selection process to determine the allocation of funding to the beneficiary organisations? (12 June 2024) The Thematic Programme for Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) is the only thematic programme with a clear actor-based mandate under the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument — Global Europe (NDICI-GE) (1). The overall aim of the programme is to strengthen CSOs as independent actors of good governance and development in their own right. The programme still relies on the three priorities of the 2012 Commission Communication (2): contributing to an enabling environment for civil society, a more inclusive CSO participation in dialogue, and strengthening CSO partner capacities. The Thematic Programme for CSOs is funded under the NDICI-GE to a total of EUR 1.51 billion. The Multiannual Indicative Programme 2021-2027 (MIP) (3) of the Thematic Programme for CSOs defines the strategy and objectives under the current multiannual financial framework. The programme complements the support provided by the EU to CSOs as implementers of other thematic and geographic programmes. Civil society organisations are subject to the same general rules on EU funding as any other entity under the Financial Regulation (4). Article 28 of the NDICI-GE defines eligible persons and entities for thematic programmes and additional eligibility criteria for applicants of EU funding may be established in the action documents with due regards to the objectives of the action and in compliance with the principles of transparency and non-discrimination. Selection criteria are established to assess the applicant’s ability to complete the proposed action and they vary in the different action documents (5) implementing the MIP of the Thematic Programme for CSOs for the period 2021-2024.
